stimuli.title: Seven employees hold seven distinct ranks (rank 1 is junior-most and rank 7 is senior-most).
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. There are exactly 1 positions between Eshan and Zoya.
2. Eshan is exactly 2 positions senior to Charu.
3. Farhan is exactly 3 positions senior to Uday.
4. Zoya is at rank 7.
5. In the stated ordering, Pooja comes before Farhan, and Farhan comes before Eshan.
stimuli.solution: rank 1: Uday; rank 2: Pooja; rank 3: Charu; rank 4: Farhan; rank 5: Eshan; rank 6: Geeta; rank 7: Zoya

stimuli.title: Seven people live on different floors of a seven-storey building. Floor 1 is the bottom floor, and floor 7 is the top floor.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z ≥ U ≤ Q = X > T, decide which conclusions follow. I: Z < X. II: U > X.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain V > Q > X < S > R, decide which conclusions follow. I: X ≤ S. II: Q > X.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain S < R ≤ X ≤ V ≥ T, decide which conclusions follow. I: S < T. II: S ≤ V.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 40 km north, then 32 km east, then 8 km south and finally 8 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² + 7x + 12 = 0. Equation II: y² − 1y + 0 = 0. Which option is always correct?
questions.explanation: Roots of x are -4 and -3; roots of y are 0 and 1. Hence x < y.

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² + 2x + 0 = 0. Equation II: y² − 3y + 0 = 0. Which option is always correct?
questions.explanation: Roots of x are -2 and 0; roots of y are 0 and 3. Hence x ≤ y.

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² + 1x − 12 = 0. Equation II: y² + 1y − 2 = 0. Which option is always correct?

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² − 5x + 6 = 0. Equation II: y² + 5y + 6 = 0. Which option is always correct?
questions.explanation: Roots of x are 2 and 3; roots of y are -3 and -2. Hence x > y.

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² − 3x + 0 = 0. Equation II: y² + 2y + 0 = 0. Which option is always correct?
